requirements.text: Each acceptance decision combines policy rules, the application score, the affordability assessment and, for secured credit, the collateral assessment, and all must be passed unless an authorised override applies.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The creditworthiness assessment relies primarily on the applicant's ability to meet the credit obligations and not predominantly on the value of the collateral.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; consistent with MCD Art. 18(3) and EBA/GL/2020/06 section 5.2.

requirements.text: The methodology, input data, assumptions and limitations of automated acceptance models are understood, and their outcomes can be explained.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; implements EBA/GL/2020/06 section 4.3.4 (technology-enabled innovation for credit decision-making).

requirements.text: All decision-engine parameters (policy rules, scorecard coefficients, cut-offs, affordability parameters) are version-controlled and changed only through the approval and model change processes.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The scorecard target is 90 days past due or default under CR-STD-110 within a 12-month (consumer) or 24-month (mortgage) performance window, and indeterminate outcomes are documented.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The development sample is drawn from the most recent through-the-door population with complete performance, and its representativeness is demonstrated with the PSI against thresholds of 0.10 and 0.25.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The discriminatory power of the scorecard is measured on an out-of-time sample and assessed against the thresholds of MV-HB-003.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where a scorecard is developed on accepted applications only, reject inference is performed, or its omission is justified by showing that selection bias has an immaterial effect on ranking.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The reject inference method and its assumptions are documented and justified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The sensitivity of the scorecard and of expected bad rates per score band to the choice of reject inference method is assessed and reported.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Cut-offs are based on the expected bad rate per score band, the target approval rate and the risk-adjusted return, within the credit risk appetite and portfolio limits.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Each cut-off proposal documents the expected approval rate, expected bad rate, expected loss and a swap-set analysis against the current cut-off.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Cut-offs and referral bands are approved by the Retail Credit Committee before implementation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Cut-offs are reviewed at least annually and after any material change in the applicant population, the scorecard or the credit risk appetite.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: An affordability assessment is performed for every application, taking into account verified income, existing credit commitments, other fixed expenses and living expenses based on reference budgets.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Income and relevant financial information are verified using independent sources.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Mortgage acceptance applies the loan-to-value, loan-to-income and debt-service-to-income limits set by national law, macroprudential measures and the credit risk appetite.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to mortgage acceptance models only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: For mortgages with an interest rate fixed for less than ten years, debt service is calculated at a stressed interest rate.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to mortgage acceptance models only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Statutory affordability limits are not overridden, and any use of a statutory exception is documented with the justification required by law.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Affordability parameters, including living expense reference budgets and stress rates, are reviewed and updated at least annually.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Low-side and high-side overrides are applied only by underwriters with delegated authority, using a reason code from a closed list and a written rationale.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Policy rules marked as non-overridable, including active default, fraud indicators and statutory affordability limits, are never overridden.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The override rate is monitored monthly per product, and a rate above 5% of decisions triggers analysis by the Model Owner and reporting to the Retail Credit Committee.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The performance of low-side overrides is tracked and compared with the expected bad rate of the scorecard at least annually.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Override reasons do not relate to protected attributes, and override decisions are included in outcome testing for disparate impact.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Front-end monitoring is performed monthly, covering application volumes, approval rates, score and characteristic stability, policy rule hit rates and override rates.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Back-end monitoring is performed at least quarterly, covering discriminatory power, observed versus expected bad rates per score band, vintage curves and early delinquency.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: A red monitoring outcome leads to a remediation plan approved by the Retail Credit Committee within three months.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Declined applicants are informed without delay and, where applicable, that the decision is based on automated processing or on a database consultation.
requirements.level_reason: Customer communication obligation of the credit origination process; evidenced in customer notification procedures, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; consistent with MCD Art. 18(5)(c).

requirements.text: Applicants subject to a decision based solely on automated processing can obtain human intervention, express their point of view and contest the decision.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to automated decisions on natural persons.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-120 v2.5) text authored for the library.
